parts.label: a
parts.technique: Variance of Poisson distribution
parts.reason: Poisson distribution is never mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements; only binomial and Normal discrete/continuous distributions are covered (S4.1, S4.2). Finding variance of W~Po(4) requires knowledge of Poisson, which is out of spec entirely.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding the mode of a binomial distribution by comparing probabilities
parts.reason: S4.1 covers use of the binomial distribution and calculating binomial probabilities. Finding the mode here is done purely by computing and comparing P(X=2) and P(X=3), a straightforward binomial probability calculation. The explicit S4.1 exclusion only bars calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables, not this mode-by-comparison method, so this part remains in spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Joint probability of independent Poisson and binomial variables
parts.reason: Requires P(W1=2) from the Poisson distribution, which is not covered anywhere in the spec statements. Even though S3.1 covers independent events, the Poisson probability itself is out of spec, so full marks cannot be earned without Poisson.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: P(X1<W1) using Poisson and binomial cumulative probabilities
parts.reason: Requires Poisson cumulative probabilities (e.g. P(W1>0), P(W1>1) etc.), which is not part of the spec. No in-spec alternative method is offered.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Mean of a continuous random variable found by integrating t·f(t) using a given pdf
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly states 'Knowledge of the probability density function is not required.' This question defines and integrates a pdf directly, which is precisely the excluded content.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding P(1<T<3) by integrating a given pdf
parts.reason: Same pdf-based technique excluded by S4.2 ('Knowledge of the probability density function is not required').

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Normal approximation to binomial for a probability derived from a pdf-based event
parts.reason: Although normal approximation to binomial with continuity correction is in S4.2, this part relies on the probability 7/16 found in part (b), which is itself derived from pdf integration excluded by S4.2. A part that only makes sense after an out-of-spec part is itself OUT.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Probability from a continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: The continuous uniform distribution is not mentioned in any spec statement; S4.1/S4.2 cover only discrete uniform, binomial and Normal distributions. This is out of spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Probability calculation for continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Same reason as (a); continuous uniform distribution not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Sketching cumulative distribution function of a continuous uniform variable
parts.reason: CDF of a continuous distribution derived from a pdf is not covered; S4.2 explicitly excludes derivation of cdf, and continuous uniform distribution itself is not mentioned.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.technique: Probability all three independent continuous uniform variables exceed a value
parts.reason: Builds on the continuous uniform distribution probability from (a)/(b), out of spec as above.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.technique: Probability the maximum of three continuous uniform variables exceeds a value
parts.reason: Same underlying continuous uniform distribution, out of spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding smallest n so that Y=0 lies in the critical region of a binomial proportion test
parts.reason: S5.2 explicitly covers conducting a hypothesis test for the proportion in the binomial distribution, including determining critical regions expressed in terms of p. This matches directly.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for a binomial proportion using a Poisson approximation
parts.reason: The mark scheme's required method approximates B(75,0.08) by Po(6) to compute the test statistic probability. Poisson approximation/distribution is not covered by any spec statement, and no in-spec alternative method (e.g. normal approximation) is offered in the mark scheme as capable of full marks here (np=6 is not suitable for the normal approximation described in S4.2, which requires p close to 0.5). Hence this part requires an out-of-spec technique.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculation
parts.reason: Poisson distribution not mentioned anywhere in the spec statements; out of spec.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.technique: Poisson cumulative probability calculation
parts.reason: Same reason; Poisson distribution excluded from spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solving for a Poisson mean parameter using binomial and Poisson distributions together
parts.reason: Relies entirely on the Poisson distribution (Po(0.15m)) and binomial-of-Poisson-events reasoning, neither of which is within the spec's coverage (Poisson never mentioned).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding a pdf constant by integrating a piecewise probability density function
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly excludes knowledge of the probability density function; this question is built entirely around integrating a defined pdf.

parts.label: (b)(i)/(ii)
parts.technique: Finding further pdf constants and probabilities from a piecewise pdf
parts.reason: Same pdf-based exclusion as (a).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Deriving the cumulative distribution function from a given pdf by integration
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly excludes derivation of the cumulative distribution function, which is exactly what this part requires.

parts.label: (a)(i)/(ii)
parts.technique: Mean and variance of a binomial distribution Y~B(20,p)
parts.reason: Although the binomial distribution is in spec (S4.1), calculating a probability p from combinatorics is fine, but the request is explicitly for mean and variance of the discrete random variable Y. S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables. This directly matches the exclusion.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Listing all samples with a given median from a small population (basic enumeration/probability)
parts.reason: This is simple systematic listing of combinations linked to conditional/mutually exclusive event reasoning (S3.1/S3.2); no excluded concept (mean/variance, pdf, sampling distribution) is invoked in this listing step itself.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of the median of a sample of counters
parts.reason: 'Sampling distribution' is a named concept not mentioned anywhere in the spec statements, making this part out of spec regardless of the underlying arithmetic being simple probability.
